identity: University of Groningen, American Studies BA, September 2026

sources.scope: University programme identity, course subject matter, published faculty-wide themes and possible minors.
2026–27 programme regulations, Arts. 3.2, 4.1, 5.1, 7.1 and 8.1, governing credit structure, required courses, sequence and transition.

curriculum: The English-taught BA comprises 60 EC each year. The 2026-entry structure in Arts. 4.1 and 5.1 assigns Stories We Live By to year one, North & South Americans to year two alongside three 10 EC courses and four rotating 5 EC topics, and a 30 EC minor, 10 EC research seminar, 10 EC faculty-wide course and 10 EC thesis to year three. The public overview places Stories We Live By in both years one and two and names Mobility, Migration, Transculturation instead of the year-three Research Seminar. The repeat of Stories and the year-three title align with elements of the 2025-entry transition in Art. 8.1. The illustrated 2026-entry case therefore uses the formal names and credit structure. Named rotating topics on the public page are examples. The first 10 EC faculty-wide course is prescribed; the second is a choice among published themes. The minor may be fulfilled through eligible choices including study abroad.
progression: Article 7.1 requires The Americas I or II before Americas III and Practice I before Practice II. The study-abroad choice requires the first year, Practice II and 30 additional second-year EC. The Research Seminar requires the first year and Practice II. The thesis requires the first year and Practice II plus 10 EC in Theories of Culture II or The Americas III. The older numbered subdivisions in the progression text are interpreted within the current course structure. No seminar-before-thesis requirement is inferred from the article.
components: Americas I: The American Century and Beyond
Stories We Live By: Mediating Identities
The Americas III: From Exploration to Early Republic
